# APPROACH TO URINARY TRACT INFECTION (UTI)

## IDSA 2025 complicated and uncomplicated UTI definition updates:

Uncomplicated UTI is an infection confined to the bladder in afebrile women or men without urinary catheter.

[Uncomplicated urinary tract infection](uncomp-uti)

Complicated UTI is an infection beyond the bladder and accompanied by symptoms including fever/other signs of systemic illness. Complicated UTI includes pyelonephritis, febrile or bacteremic UTI, catheter-associated (CAUTI).

[Complicated UTI without catheter](complicated-uti-no-catheter)
[Complicated UTI catheter associated](complicated-uti-catheter-associated)
[Acute prostatitis](acute-bact-prostatitis)

For patients presenting with septic shock from a suspected urinary tract infection: see [Sepsis, urinary tract infection](sepsis-urosepsis) Asymptomatic bacteriuria occurs in patients who have bacteria in the urine but do not have symptoms of a urinary tract infection.

[Asymptomatic bacteriuria](asymp-bacteriuria)

Patients at risk of sexually transmitted infections should be assessed for treatment:

[Sexually Transmitted Infections and HIV Exposure](sexually-transmitted-infection)

Candida urinary tract infections are discussed elsewhere:

[Candida urinary tract infections](candida-uti)
